item.title: Neeraj Chopra takes silver, Yashvir wins bronze as India secure two medals in javelin at CWG
item.description: Neeraj, the 28-year-old Tokyo Olympic champion, was not at his best in difficult weather but still managed a season-best throw of 85.83m in his second attempt to finish second.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: PM Modi: I forgive those who abused me & my mom, our job to guide them
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will forgive young protesters accused of abuse. He stated these misguided children need guidance and correction, not punishment. The Prime Minister believes punishing them will not change circumstances effectively. Mistakes made at a young age present an opportunity for correction and societal acceptance. This decision indicates that cases against these youngsters will likely be withdrawn.
item.dc:creator: KUMAR RAKESH

item.title: ‘Dhurandhar’ gangster’s brother shot in Karachi
item.description: Zubair Baloch, brother of jailed gangster Uzair Baloch, was critically wounded in a drive-by shooting. Two masked assailants on a motorcycle opened fire, striking him in the chest and abdomen. Zubair was rushed to Civil Hospital Karachi for emergency surgery after the attack. Police are investigating personal enmity and potential gang war resurgence as motives. The incident occurred in Karachi's Lyari neighborhood, a historic hub of organized crime.
item.dc:creator: RAJ SHEKHAR JHA

item.title: Amid opposition protest, Lok Sabha passes births & deaths bill
item.description: The Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, without any debate. Opposition members disrupted Rajya Sabha proceedings, preventing any business from being transacted. The bill aims to make delayed registrations of births and deaths more stringent. Congress and SP MPs raised issues concerning police actions and alleged temple donation theft. The Rajya Sabha was ultimately adjourned for the entire day.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Ethanol kept petrol prices lower: Govt
item.description: Ethanol blending saved consumers nearly thirty rupees per litre on petrol. Global crude prices reached one hundred thirty-five dollars a barrel recently. The government kept fuel prices unchanged for seventy-five days initially. E20 petrol now costs one hundred two rupees per litre in Delhi. Allegations of foodgrain diversion for ethanol were also rejected.
item.dc:creator: ATUL MATHUR

item.title: When a district in Florida's Everglades used robot rabbits to eliminate Burmese pythons
item.description: Florida is employing AI-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons. These solar-powered decoys mimic prey using heat and scent to lure snakes. When a python is detected, officials are alerted to remove the invasive species. This technology complements the annual Python Challenge, which has removed thousands of snakes. These efforts aim to control the python population impacting native wildlife.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Tahir Hussain gets life for IB staffer’s killing in 2020 riots
item.description: A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment. They were convicted for the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma. The court found Sharma was lynched solely on account of his religion during the 2020 riots. While the prosecution sought the death penalty, it was declined by the judge. The judge considered educational backgrounds as a mitigating factor for the convicts.
item.dc:creator: KOUSHIKI SAHA

item.title: 16.4% deleted in Haryana draft roll; 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh
item.description: Draft voter rolls in Haryana and Andhra Pradesh reveal significant exclusions. Over sixteen percent of Haryana's electorate and over ten percent in Andhra were removed. Reasons cited include deaths, permanent shifts, and multiple registrations. However, genuine voters can still be added during the claims period. This process allows for corrections and additions to the electoral rolls.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN AND SAMDANI MN

item.title: NYC banned Motoclick, now Mamdani targets Uber Eats, DoorDash over 'hidden' tip buttons
item.description: New York City's delivery workers have gained over one hundred million dollars. This increase follows new rules requiring clear tipping options at checkout. Apps like Uber Eats and DoorDash redesigned their interfaces after city enforcement actions. Workers now see significantly higher hourly earnings and more deliveries completed. The administration continues its efforts to improve app-based worker conditions.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Monsoon likely to be ‘below normal’ in Aug-Sept: IMD
item.description: India's monsoon rainfall is expected to be below normal during August and September. This forecast is influenced by the continuing risk of El Niño, which often weakens the monsoon. July rainfall, however, turned out to be normal due to plentiful showers in central India. These showers helped reduce the overall monsoon rainfall deficit significantly by the end of July.
item.dc:creator: VISHWA MOHAN

item.title: Michigan woman sues Toll Brothers over access to her 19-acre property
item.description: A woman from Michigan has initiated legal action against Toll Brothers concerning their wastewater management and access rights. Her property, undeveloped, is situated between two upcoming luxury housing estates. The lawsuit alleges that the developers have disregarded her property rights and neglected environmental regulations. She aims to reinstate her access easement and challenge the site plan approvals.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 13-year-old turns peanut shells into pesticide remover, eyes $25K prize
item.description: Thirteen-year-old Minnesota student Arika Kundu has designed a method that uses discarded peanut shells to help remove pesticide residues from fresh fruits and vegetables. Her project, called LIGNEX, has made her one of 10 finalists in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge. She will now compete for the $25,000 grand prize with guidance from a 3M scientist.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: US plans $100K fee on foreign students: What it means for engineers
item.description: The US government is reportedly considering a $100,000 fee for foreign students seeking post-graduation work. This proposed fee targets the Optional Practical Training program, impacting many international graduates. This follows a significant H-1B visa fee hike imposed on sponsoring companies last year. Indian engineers, who dominate H-1B approvals, face increased challenges in securing US careers. The new measures may significantly narrow career paths for many skilled foreign professionals.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: 'Pak-trained Mujahideen turned guns inwards': MEA slams Islamabad over PoK crackdown
item.description: India condemned Pakistan's admission of training and arming militants who have turned against the state. The Ministry of External Affairs also criticized Pakistan's harsh crackdown on protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. Over forty civilians were reportedly killed during the violent suppression of peaceful demonstrations. India stated that Pakistan's actions exposed its disdain for the region's innocent inhabitants.
item.dc:creator: AYUSH PANDEY

item.title: How Travis Kelce turned criticism into one of the NFL's greatest careers ever
item.description: For Travis Kelce, constructive criticism serves as a catalyst for growth and improvement. His passion for football, established long before his fame, has fueled his journey. Despite setbacks, such as not making the 2025 NFL playoffs, Kelce stresses the importance of embracing feedback and maintaining daily dedication to progress, especially for younger generations.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Connor McDavid faces backlash over comments on Maple Leafs' Gavin McKenna
item.description: Connor McDavid faced criticism from Sid Seixeiro regarding his remarks on Gavin McKenna. Seixeiro argued McDavid does not understand Toronto's intense media scrutiny. He believes Edmonton's media environment differs significantly from Toronto's pressures. McKenna, the top draft pick, faces high expectations from fans and media. The prospect signed a contract and will play alongside Auston Matthews.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: How family sacrifice fueled Usain Bolt's rise to sprinting greatness worldwide
item.description: Usain Bolt’s incredible career was built on more than speed. His parents, Wellesley and Jennifer Bolt, helped him stay disciplined, focused and humble from childhood to Olympic glory. Even after becoming the fastest man in history, Bolt remained deeply connected to his family. His story continues to inspire because it shows that lasting success begins with love, sacrifice and strong values.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: SC slaps Rs 1 lakh fine on Rajasthan government for harassing official
item.description: The Supreme Court has ordered Rajasthan to pay one lakh rupees to a government official. This payment is compensation for harassment caused by political interference in a prosecution sanction. The court criticized the joint secretary of the former chief minister for undue influence. Such interference was deemed a blatant display of political dictate by the state. The official was unnecessarily dragged to court, prompting the court's strong observations.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Jharkhand zoo hatches cobra and sand boa eggs through artificial incubation first time
item.description: The Bhagwan Birsa Biological Park successfully incubated Spectacled Cobra eggs artificially. Five healthy hatchlings emerged after a seventy-day incubation period under controlled conditions. The park also welcomed eight Sand Boa hatchlings during this conservation initiative. This success highlights the importance of scientific management in reptile breeding programs. The hatchlings are now under close observation and veterinary care.

item.title: CWG: India strike double gold in judo as Asmita Dey, Harsh Singh make history
item.description: Asmita created history by becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal after defeating Canada's Heidi Quach in the women's 48kg final.

item.title: Hockey jersey row: Dilip Tirkey questions process, his federation cites precedent
item.description: Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey questioned the jersey colour change process. He stated the decision lacked executive board discussion and his prior knowledge. Executive director RK Srivastava defended the saffron kit based on technical and performance factors. Other board members also raised concerns about transparency and accountability. This controversy emerges amid ongoing governance scrutiny for Hockey India.
item.dc:creator: ARNAB LALL SEAL

item.title: 'I felt that everything was over': Asmita remembers late father after historic judo gold
item.description: Asmita Dey secured India's first judo gold medal at the Commonwealth Games. She defeated Canada's Heidi Quach in a gripping golden score final match. This historic victory came after overcoming personal tragedy and immense dedication. Harsh Singh also won a gold medal in the men's 60kg judo event. These twin triumphs marked a significant breakthrough for Indian judo.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: MAGA piles on to Morocco as Trump twits Spain over Ceuta
item.description: The migrant surge into Ceuta is escalating into a geopolitical flashpoint. President Trump is using the crisis to reinforce his border security message. This event is also fueling online conspiracy theories linking it to wider international disputes. US officials have intervened in Spain's domestic politics regarding immigration policies. The situation highlights strained US-Spain relations and territorial claims over Ceuta.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Heaps of cash & gold, 242 vehicles & more: WB CM Suvendu lists Tulu Mondal's assets
item.description: Authorities have confiscated more than Rs 150 crore in cash, gold, and various assets belonging to mining mogul Tulu Mondal. This haul comprises numerous vehicles, petrol pumps, and several properties. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari attributed the rise of this illegal operation to the former Chief Minister, claiming that illegal stone mining led to a staggering Rs 15,000 crore revenue loss over a stretch of fifteen years.
item.dc:creator: KAUSHIK PRADHAN

item.description: Lawmakers from both parties, along with industry trade groups, have raised concerns over a section of the legislation that would allow Trump to impose hefty tariffs on countries that buy significant volumes of Russian oil and gas.

item.title: Rashmika Mandanna suffers major hip injury on set; doctors advise six weeks of rest
item.description: Actress Rashmika Mandanna sustained a major hip injury while filming an intense dance sequence. Doctors have advised her a complete rest period of six weeks for recovery. This injury will likely impact her ongoing film schedules and endorsement commitments. Mandanna is currently working on several big-budget films and numerous brand endorsements. Fans are sending well wishes for her swift return to full fitness.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Mukesh Khanna says CJP doesn't represent students or Gen Z
item.description: Veteran actor Mukesh Khanna has weighed in on the ongoing controversy surrounding the recent Gen Z protests, reacting to the self-styled Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and backing criticism over the alleged use of abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The actor described some protesters as "cockroaches" and alleged that they did not represent genuine students.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Perfect 5-0! Indian boxers storm into CWG finals after dominant semifinal sweep
item.description: India's boxing contingent achieved a flawless 5-0 record in the semifinals. Five Indian boxers have now secured spots in the gold medal bouts. Arundhati Choudhary defeated the defending champion in a significant upset victory. Jaismine Lamboria and Preeti Pawar also advanced with dominant performances. Ankush Panghal and Jadumani Singh completed the perfect sweep for India.

item.description: The scheme will be implemented through FY2030-31 with an aim to harness India's vast offshore energy resources - in what the government has termed as a modern day Samudra Manthan.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: 'Clarify algorithmic bias': Govt summons Meta's global team over PM Modi post
item.description: India's government has summoned Meta's global team to discuss Prime Minister Modi's post. Officials will question the social media giant on algorithmic bias and content moderation. Meta's global representatives will also appear before a parliamentary panel for scrutiny. Hyderabad police have also registered cases against Meta India's head. This marks an escalation in the government's oversight of the company's practices.
item.dc:creator: AYUSH PANDEY

item.title: Russia hits Ukraine military cargo vessel near Odesa as Kyiv targets oil refinery
item.description: Russia claimed striking a vessel near Odesa carrying military cargo. Ukraine reported hitting Russia's Volgograd oil refinery and port infrastructure. Both nations are increasingly targeting logistics and supply chains. This escalation highlights the Black Sea's crucial role in the ongoing conflict. Ukraine also continues its campaign against Russian logistics targets.
item.dc:creator: AYUSH PANDEY

item.title: India likely to play waiting game with Bumrah for Sri Lanka Tests | Exclusive
item.description: The 32-year-old was picked in the Shubman Gill-led squad for the series, but subject to fitness clearance. Bumrah missed the third ODI against England at Lord's due to an "impact injury" to his left knee but looked very sharp in the two fixtures he did play.

item.title: Vedika Pinto's sea-facing Mumbai home with Goan-Portuguese charm
item.description: 'Musafir Cafe' actor Vedika Pinto gives an intimate tour of her 4000 sq ft Mumbai home, blending contemporary design with Goan-Portuguese touches that pay homage to her father's ancestry. From a restored newspaper artwork bought in Beirut to a painting with a cheeky "Green Choli" backstory, Vedika opens up about the stories behind her home's most striking corners.

item.title: 'Done by BJP goons': CJP's Dipke responds after injured Delhi cops' kin seek justice
item.description: Families of the injured Delhi Police officers are advocating for a discussion in Parliament regarding their pain. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke suggested a deliberate effort to target students amid the protests, expressing concern for the hurt officers while also questioning how students were being treated. The families presented proof of injuries and extensive damage, asserting that anti-social groups had incited the violence.
